description: stats prints line, word and character counts for a text file
steps: Run: python3 app.py stats tests/sample.txt
Confirm lines, words and chars are printed

description: stats --json prints exactly one JSON object with lines, words and chars
steps: Run: python3 app.py stats tests/sample.txt --json
Confirm stdout parses as a single JSON object with those three keys

description: stats --csv prints a header row followed by the values row
steps: Run: python3 app.py stats tests/sample.txt --csv
Confirm the first line is the header lines,words,chars
Confirm the second line holds the matching values

description: stats --top N lists the N most frequent words, most frequent first
steps: Run: python3 app.py stats tests/sample.txt --top 3
Confirm the words are ordered by descending frequency, not alphabetically

description: a missing input file exits 1 with a one-line error on stderr and no traceback
steps: Run: python3 app.py stats does-not-exist.txt
Confirm the exit code is 1
Confirm stderr holds a short error message and no Python traceback

description: stats --csv --top N prints word,count rows with a word,count header
steps: Run: python3 app.py stats tests/sample.txt --csv --top 3
Confirm the header is word,count
Confirm each following row is a word and its count, most frequent first

description: an unrecognised flag exits 2 with a usage message rather than being ignored
steps: Run: python3 app.py stats tests/sample.txt --nonsense
Confirm the exit code is 2
Confirm a usage message names the unknown flag

description: stats reads from stdin when the path is - and honours --json
steps: Run: printf 'a b\nc d\n' | python3 app.py stats - --json
Confirm one JSON object is printed with lines 2, words 4, chars 8

description: plain output is ANSI-coloured on a terminal and uncoloured when piped
steps: Run the plain command attached to a terminal and confirm the labels carry ANSI colour codes
Run the same command with stdout piped to a file and confirm the file holds no ANSI escape sequences

description: a 200 MB input is processed without the process exceeding 100 MB of resident memory
steps: Generate a 200 MB text file
Run stats over it while measuring peak resident memory
Confirm the peak stays under 100 MB, i.e. the file is streamed rather than read whole

description: the verification battery is green and the work is pushed to origin
steps: Run: bash .claude/hooks/verify.sh
Confirm every check passes
Commit the work and push it to origin/main
